Překousaný nebo poškozený kabel: co děla: Chewed or damaged cable: what to do?
Překousaný, přiskřípnutý nebo naříznutý: A chewed, pinched or cut cable can be live even if the appliance still works. What to do straight away, what not to touch and when to call an electrician @@V city_in@@.
: Překousaný nebo poškozený kabel: co dě: : Chewed or damaged cable: what to do
Kabely v domácnosti nejčastěji poškodí d: Cables at home are most often damaged by pets or rodents, furniture pushed against a wall or doors that trap a cord. If the insulation is chewed through or cracked, you may see bare wire – and it stays live as long as the cable is plugged in.
Nebezpečný může být i kabel, na kterém z: A cable can be dangerous even when there’s hardly anything to see on the outside – the insulation only needs to be crushed or nicked inside. So don’t touch the damaged spot, and keep children and pets away from it.
Pokud jde o šňůru spotřebiče nebo prodlu: If it’s an appliance cord or an extension lead and the plug is undamaged and easy to reach, unplug it. Keep your hands dry, stand on a dry floor and pull the plug body, never the cable.
Když vede poškozený kabel pevně ve zdi n: If the damaged cable is fixed in a wall or trunking, if the plug is damaged too, or if you can’t reach it safely, switch off that circuit’s breaker at the consumer unit. If you don’t know which one, switch off the main switch. Don’t plug in an appliance with a damaged cord again.
Izolepa kabelu vrátí jen vzhled, ne bezp: Tape restores the look of a cable, not its safety. It doesn’t restore the original insulation or strength, it loosens over time and the damage underneath can get worse. A taped cable also looks fine, so it’s easy to forget about. Cutting and joining cables at home is just as risky.
Elektrikář posoudí, jak daleko poškození: An electrician assesses how far the damage goes. For an appliance cord or extension lead, replacing the whole cable is usually safest. For wiring in a wall, they check the rest of the circuit and test the installation after the repair. If it’s an appliance, they’ll advise whether a repair is worth it or it belongs with a service centre.
Když proud někoho zasáhl: If someone gets an electric shock
Na zasaženého nesahejte, dokud je ve sty: Don’t touch the person while they’re in contact with the conductor. First cut the power at the breaker or main switch, then call your local emergency number. Even if they seem fine, they should be checked by a doctor.

Proč vypadává jistič v rozvaděči?: Why does my breaker keep tripping?
Jistič, který opakovaně vypadává, vás na: A breaker that keeps tripping is warning you about something. The most common causes, what you can safely try yourself and when it’s time to call an electrician @@V city_in@@.
: Proč vypadává jistič v rozvaděči: : Why does my breaker keep tripping
Jistič chrání, nevypadává jen tak: A breaker protects you – it doesn’t trip for no reason
Jistič vypne okruh, když jím teče větší: A breaker switches a circuit off when more current flows than the circuit is designed for, or when there’s a short circuit. The RCD – usually next to the breakers, with a test button – watches for something else: it trips when some current leaks out of the circuit, for example through moisture or damaged insulation. Both protect you and the installation. If they trip, something is wrong somewhere.
na jednom okruhu běží naráz víc výkonnýc: several high-power appliances run on one circuit at once, such as a kettle, a microwave and an electric heater.
zkrat nebo poškozená izolace uvnitř spot: a short circuit or damaged insulation inside the appliance or its cord.
voda v zásuvce nebo krabici, venkovní zá: water in a socket or junction box, an outdoor socket after rain, a damp bathroom or basement.
uvolněný spoj, poškozený kabel ve zdi ne: a loose connection, a damaged cable in the wall or old wiring at the end of its life.
Vadný může být i samotný jistič nebo chr: The breaker or RCD itself can be faulty too – but only testing will tell.
Odpojte ze zásuvek na postiženém okruhu: Unplug every appliance on the affected circuit and try resetting the breaker once. If it holds, plug the appliances back in one at a time. Stop using the one that makes it trip again.
Když jistič vypadne hned, i když je všec: If the breaker trips straight away even with everything unplugged, or keeps tripping, don’t keep resetting it. Never hold the lever up by force and never swap the breaker for a “bigger” one – the circuit would no longer be protected. If you smell burning, hear crackling or see scorch marks, leave the breaker off and call a professional straight away.
Elektrikář okruh proměří: zkontroluje st: An electrician tests the circuit: insulation, connections, breakers and RCDs, and what is running on it. Based on the results they propose a fix – repairing the specific fault, splitting an overloaded circuit, a dedicated circuit for high-power appliances, adding RCD protection or updating the consumer unit. You’ll get an explanation of why the breaker was tripping and what we recommend next.
Co dělat, když zásuvka hřeje nebo jiskří: What to do if a socket gets hot or sparks?
Teplá zásuvka, jiskření při zapojování n: A warm socket, sparks when plugging in or a smell of burnt plastic are warning signs you shouldn’t ignore. What to do straight away and why an electrician @@V city_in@@ should check it.
: Co dělat, když zásuvka hřeje nebo jisk: : What to do if a socket gets hot or sparks
Zásuvka ani zástrčka by při běžném provo: Neither a socket nor a plug should feel noticeably warm in normal use. If they’re hot, sparking, crackling, smell burnt, or the plastic around them is discoloured or warped, a fault is already happening. Don’t wait to see if it happens again.
V rozvaděči vypněte jistič okruhu, na kt: Switch off the breaker for that socket’s circuit at the consumer unit. If you don’t know which one, switch off the main switch.
Teprve potom vytáhněte zástrčku. Pokud j: Only then pull out the plug. If the socket is hot or damaged, let it cool down first.
Zásuvku do kontroly nepoužívejte a upozo: Don’t use the socket until it’s been checked, and tell everyone at home not to switch the breaker back on.
Když se objeví kouř nebo plamen, odejdět: If there’s smoke or flames, leave the room and call your local emergency number. Never use water on live equipment.
Nejčastěji jde o uvolněný nebo zoxidovan: Most often it’s a loose or corroded terminal connection, worn contacts that hold the plug loosely, or overloading – for example high-power appliances on adaptors and extension leads. A damaged appliance plug can also be to blame.
Špatný spoj klade proudu odpor a zahřívá: A bad connection resists the current and heats up. The heat gradually damages the insulation and surrounding plastic, so the problem won’t fix itself – quite the opposite. It’s also a warning sign if a plug sits loosely in the socket, or a lamp flickers when you touch its plug.
Nezapojujte do jedné zásuvky přes rozboč: Don’t run several high-power appliances such as a heater, a kettle or a hair dryer from one socket through an adaptor.
Nezapojujte prodlužovačky a rozbočovače: Don’t daisy-chain extension leads and adaptors.
Prodlužovačku na navijáku při větším zat: Fully unwind a cable reel under heavy load – a coiled cable heats up more.
Nepoužívejte zásuvku s prasklým nebo uvo: Don’t use a socket with a cracked or loose cover.
Elektrikář zásuvku otevře, zkontroluje s: An electrician opens the socket, checks the terminals and supply wires, and repairs or replaces it as needed. They also check the plug of the appliance that was connected and the load on the whole circuit. If the socket is regularly overloaded, they’ll suggest extra sockets or a dedicated circuit so it doesn’t happen again.
Kdy je potřeba revize elektroinstalace?: When do you need an electrical safety inspection?
Revize ověří, že je elektroinstalace bez: An inspection confirms your wiring is safe. When it’s worth having one and how to prepare – for flats and houses @@V city_in@@.
: Kdy je potřeba revize elektroinstalace: : When do you need an electrical safety inspection
Revize je odborná prohlídka elektroinsta: An electrical inspection is a professional check of your installation, with measurements and tests. A qualified electrician carries it out and sums up the result in a written report: the condition of the installation, any faults found and whether it is safe to use.
Revize sama nic neopravuje. Zjištěné záv: The inspection itself doesn’t fix anything. Faults go into the report, and putting them right is the next step – so the report gives you a clear list of what needs doing.
Nová elektroinstalace se musí před uvede: New wiring should be tested before it’s put into use, and so should significant changes to an existing installation – a renovation, new circuits or a new consumer unit. What exactly is required depends on local rules, and your electrician can tell you.

Kdy se revize vyplatí: When an inspection is worth it
revizní zpráva ukáže skutečný stav rozvo: the report shows the real condition of the wiring. The buyer knows what they’re getting, and the seller has it documented.
hliníkové vodiče nebo starší rozvody bez: aluminium wiring or older circuits without an earth conductor, once common, are worth checking even if they still work.
při škodě způsobené závadou elektroinsta: after damage caused by an electrical fault, such as a fire, your insurer may look into the condition of the installation. Your policy terms say what exactly they require.
a po jakémkoli poškození, kdy si nejste: and after any damage where you’re not sure whether the wiring was affected.
Lhůtu další pravidelné revize doporučí r: The electrician recommends when the next inspection is due in the report itself, based on the type of property and how it’s used. So you don’t need to guess – just check your last report. If you don’t have one, that alone is a good reason to book an inspection.
Zajistěte přístup k rozvaděči a do všech: Make sure the consumer unit and every room are accessible. Have any previous reports or installation documents ready. The power usually needs to be switched off for a while during the inspection, so expect a short outage.
